newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose slightly against the dollar on Thursday in thin trading, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet today and the shekel traded in a tight range with slightly more conversions of foreign currency into shekels," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The business sector was converting foreign currency for end-of-the-month payments while other investors were repaying foreign currency loans linked to the yen and Swiss franc," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5400 shekels compared with 3.5460 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7854 against 3.7823 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 2.9961 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9836 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9331 shekels compared with 1.9238 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5390 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
